Deep in the forest lived a girl named Ella, who wove winter nests for small animals from fallen leaves each day. One snowy night, she rescued a frozen bluebird. When the bird awoke, it repaid her by spitting out a glowing seed. Ella buried the seed in the moss, and by the next day, it had grown into a Crystal tree. Silver fruit hung among its branches like dewdrops, each reflecting what people desired most in their hearts.

When the greedy lord heard about it, he stormed into the forest with an axe. But as he struck the trunk, all the fruit suddenly shattered at once, reflecting thousands of disappointed eyes—the eyes of every impoverished person in his domain. The Crystal tree dissolved into mist, leaving only the plainest fruit to roll into Ella's hand. Within it was a vision of the entire forest flourishing.

Ella finally understood. She gently buried the fruit beside the stream. In the morning light, glowing flowers bloomed all along the bank. They bore no fruit, but allowed everyone who passed to see their heart's true desire. From then on, no one in the forest fought over treasure, because everyone Discovered that the most precious magic had already quietly taken root within their hearts.
